In-source CID converts ADP-ribosyl to phosphoribosyl-H2O peptides that are more amenable to HCD-dependent peptide sequencing, providing an alternative method for acceptor site determination when ETD-based methods are not available.

Interconversion of ADPr peptides to their phosphoribosyl-H2O derivatives increased with increasing source voltage (up to 50V), as judged by monitoring the corresponding modification loss ([adenosine monophosphate/AMP]+) and the number of identified phosphoribosyl-H2O peptide identifications. The average Xcorr increased from 1.36 (ADPr) to 2.26 (phosphoribosyl-H2O), similar to that achieved with EThcD for ADPr peptides (2.29).
